chunks: Then return the gaze twice. The gaze will turn back to you dazed and weary.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the gaze returns dazed and tired in Surah Al-Mulk?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse illustrates the psychological torment of the disbelievers who, despite being commanded to look around for a way out, find their gaze returning in a state of 'khāsi'an' (humiliated) and 'ḥasīr' (exhausted/frustrated). This reflects the futility of seeking relief from Allah when the source of their confinement is ultimately His decree, emphasizing that their blindness was self-inflicted through denial of divine signs.
